name: Assembly

attributes.attribute: Irish ritual assembly held at regular intervals
site of trade in horses and cattle
sacred hill that hosted a Beltane Óenach
goddess whose site hosted a Lughnasa Óenach

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Assembly is the English term that translates the Irish Óenach. The Óenach was the Irish ritual assembly. At regular intervals, the Celtic peoples of Ireland gathered at sacred places. They held seasonal rituals that honored the natural cycle and restored the ancient union of the tribe. The assembly served many purposes beyond religion. People traded horses and cattle. Young people met and courted. Laborers were hired. Contracts were made between distant parties. An important Óenach took place on Beltane at the sacred hill of Uisneach in the center of Ireland. Another took place on Lughnasa at the site sacred to the goddess Tailtiu.
objective: Establish the Óenach as the Irish ritual assembly for seasonal rites and public business.
key_results: Óenach assemblies were held at regular intervals.
They were sites of trade in horses and cattle and of courtship and hiring.
A Beltane Óenach met at the hill of Uisneach.
A Lughnasa Óenach met at the site sacred to the goddess Tailtiu.
